findings.F1: About half of the book's gain is the market's own rise: its mean daily return is 0.000667, of which 0.000345 is the position held times the coin's mean daily return. Timing adds about 0.0004 (the position's gain before costs is 0.000742).
findings.F2: The gain sits in a few large days and trades. Without its best 1 % of days (28 of 2898), the book's mean daily return falls from 0.000667 to -0.000027. The top 5 % of trades sum to 4835 of the 6123 summed percent of all 2239 trades (79 %). The median trade earns 0.28 % against a mean of 2.73 %.
findings.F3: One year carries much of it. 2020 averages 0.00291 a day. Without 2020 the book's mean is 0.000346, about the market part alone, and 2018 (-0.000506) and 2022 (-0.000675) lose.

findings.F6: The size of the 20-day run-up does not grade the 5-day move. By quintile of the 20-day return, the top quintile earns +0.43 % (t 0.84) against +1.02 % (t 2.10) for the fourth. Within the top quintile, breakout cells earn +0.59 % (101 cases) against +0.40 % for the others (469).
findings.F7: The effect is not carried by one coin, but XMR fails. At 5 days after the first breakout bar, five coins have an unusual move of +0.52 % to +1.81 % (ZEC t 1.85) and XMR has -0.19 %. XMR's book earns 0.000162 a day, less than its market part of 0.000383.
findings.F8: Days in position are followed by a next-day unusual return of +0.146 % (6083 bars), days out by -0.086 % (8417 bars).

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 20 days. The more times the level held and the further the close above it, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A close through a repeatedly held 90-day level is a reason to stay long for weeks rather than days, without requiring a strong prior month.
ideas.name: resistance break, weeks-long continuation
